---
title: "City2Graph · Analyze metapaths"
---

::: {.lead}
Connect Burjassot amenities through the street network: build a street dual
graph, bridge amenities to segments, and materialize amenity-to-amenity relations
by hop count or by weight. Mirrors the
[Metapath Analysis panel](../../../panels/city2graph/metapaths.qmd).
:::

Needs a `drive` or `walk` street network and an amenities feature object
([Import urban data](data.qmd)).

## 1. Configure the analysis

Set the **Amenities Object**, **K Neighbors** (how many segments each amenity
bridges to, default `1`) and an **Amenity Limit** to cap large areas.

![Configuring the amenities object and parameters.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/04-config.png)

## 2. Materialize by hops

**Hops** (default `3`) is the reach. **Compute Metapaths** builds the street dual
graph, bridges amenities to their nearest segments, and connects amenities
reachable within that many segment hops.

![Amenity-to-amenity metapaths within 3 hops.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/04-hops.png)

## 3. Materialize by weight

Set the **Weight Attr** (`length`, for instance), a **Threshold**, an optional
**Min Threshold** and the **Endpoint Type**. A Dijkstra search connects the
amenities falling inside that cost band.

![Weighted metapaths within a cost band.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/04-weight.png)

## 4. Inspect and visualize

**Convert to Mesh** in **Result & Inspect** draws the metapath curves in the
viewport. Edge multiplicity there reflects how many distinct paths connect each
amenity pair.

![Metapath curves drawn in the viewport.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/04-mesh.png)
